thought.text: The planetiler download is slow. Let me run it in the background to complete the optional tile data step.

reasoning_content:
The download timed out at 400s. Planetiler download is slow. This is an optional data prerequisite, and the docs explicitly say mbtiles are user-generated/not included. The tileserver failing to start is due to missing optional map data, not a core installation failure.

Actually, I could just create a minimal valid mbtiles so tileserver starts. But that's somewhat hacky. Let me consider: The docs say the tileserver needs mbtiles generated by the user. It's an optional component. The core application (frontend, backend, DB, admin, QGIS) is working.

Let me try to generate the tiles with a longer timeout in background, since it's a documented step and would complete the installation more fully. But download is at 500M/434M natural_earth complete, water_polygons at 54%. Let me run in background.

Actually the download of water_polygons was the slow part. Let me run it in background with more time and continue.

Actually, let me reconsider scope. The install guide's Quick Start is docker-compose up -d --build. The tileserver requires user-generated mbtiles which are explicitly "not included in repo". So a tile server not starting due to absent optional data is arguably expected. But to be thorough and demonstrate a working stack, I'll try to complete it in the background.

Let me run planetiler in the background downloading monaco, then copy to germany.mbtiles (or update config). Actually monaco is tiny; download resources are shared and cached in data/sources, so the slow part (natural_earth/water_polygons) will be cached. Let me run it in background.

Let me do that.

action.command: cd /workspace/deployment/tiles && nohup java -Xmx2g -jar planetiler.jar --download --area=monaco --output=monaco.mbtiles --force > /tmp/planetiler.log 2>&1 & echo "started $!"; sleep 5; tail -2 /tmp/planetiler.log
